Replace each `___` with code, remove `#| eval: false` and run the chunk. Write your answer under each chunk.

The data are life expectancy values from Gapminder. Put `gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv` in the `data` folder of the project.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
gapminder_wide <- read_csv(here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv"))
```

## One row per country, one column per year

```{r}
#| label: look-wide
gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`, `2023`)
```

## Wide to long: pivot_longer()

Run this chunk. We wrote it together in class.

```{r}
#| label: make-long
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  )

gapminder_long
```

## Your turn 3: change the type of year

Turn `year` into a whole number, then draw the line plot again.

```{r}
#| label: turn-3
#| eval: false
gapminder_long |>
  mutate(year = ___(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

Answer: the function is [YOUR ANSWER HERE].

Run this chunk. It rewrites `gapminder_long` with the fix inside the pipeline.

```{r}
#| label: make-long-fixed
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))
```

## Long to wide: pivot_wider()

`table2` comes with the tidyr package. Run this chunk.

```{r}
#| label: table2-example
table2 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = count)
```
